quests.instruction: Which of these years is a leap year?
quests.hint: A leap year can be divided exactly by 4.
quests.explanation: 2028 divides exactly by 4, because 2028 ÷ 4 = 507, so it is a leap year. 2026 and 2030 do not divide exactly by 4.
quests.funFact: People born on 29 February are sometimes called leaplings.

quests.instruction: In a leap year, what date comes the day after 28 February?
quests.hint: A leap year has one extra day in its shortest month.
quests.explanation: In a leap year, February has 29 days, so the day after 28 February is 29 February.
quests.funFact: A leap year is needed because the Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to travel around the Sun.

quests.instruction: How many days are there from 1 February to 1 March in a leap year?
quests.hint: How many days does February have in a leap year?
quests.explanation: From 1 February to 1 March is the whole month of February, which has 29 days in a leap year.
quests.funFact: The year 1900 was not a leap year, but the year 2000 was, because of a special rule for century years.

quests.instruction: In a normal year, how many days are there from 15 January to 15 March?
quests.hint: Count from 15 January to 15 February, then on to 15 March.
quests.explanation: 15 January to 15 February is 31 days. 15 February to 15 March is 28 days in a normal year. 31 + 28 = 59 days.
quests.funFact: Julius Caesar introduced the idea of leap years in the Roman calendar in the year 45 BC.

quests.instruction: A library book is due 21 days after 20 November. What is the due date?
quests.hint: November has 30 days. Count to the end of the month, then into December.
quests.explanation: 20 November to 30 November is 10 days. 11 more days reach 11 December.
quests.funFact: Before computers, libraries stamped a due date inside each book.

quests.instruction: A seed was planted on 25 May and sprouted 10 days later. On what date did it sprout?
quests.hint: May has 31 days.
quests.explanation: 25 May to 31 May is 6 days. 4 more days reach 4 June.
quests.funFact: Seeds sprout faster in warm weather than in cold weather.

quests.instruction: A club meets every Tuesday. Its first meeting is on Tuesday 3 June. What is the date of the third meeting?
quests.hint: Meetings are 7 days apart.
quests.explanation: The second meeting is on 10 June and the third meeting is on 17 June.
quests.funFact: Some public holidays are fixed to a weekday, such as the first Monday of a month.

quests.instruction: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be in 10 days?
quests.hint: Take away 7 days first. What is left?
quests.explanation: 10 days is 1 week and 3 days. A week later is Wednesday again, and 3 more days is Saturday.
quests.funFact: Counting in whole weeks first makes long gaps on a calendar much easier.

quests.instruction: Today is Monday. What day of the week was it 12 days ago?
quests.hint: Go back 7 days first, then count back the rest.
quests.explanation: 7 days ago was also a Monday. Going back 5 more days from Monday gives Wednesday.
quests.funFact: To go back in time on a calendar, take away whole weeks first and then count back the days that are left.

quests.instruction: A night flight leaves on Friday at 11:45 PM and lasts 4 hours 30 minutes. If the clocks at both airports show the same time, when does it land?
quests.hint: Count the minutes to midnight first.
quests.explanation: 11:45 PM to midnight is 15 minutes. The other 4 hours 15 minutes after midnight make 4:15 AM, which is on Saturday.
quests.funFact: An overnight flight is often called a red-eye, because passengers can arrive tired with red eyes.

quests.instruction: A shop closes at 9:00 PM on Saturday and reopens at 8:30 AM on Monday. For how long is it closed?
quests.hint: Count to the same time on Sunday first, then on to Monday morning.
quests.explanation: Saturday 9:00 PM to Sunday 9:00 PM is 24 hours. Sunday 9:00 PM to Monday 8:30 AM is 11 hours 30 minutes. So the shop is closed for 35 hours 30 minutes.
quests.funFact: In some countries many shops close all day on Sunday.

quests.instruction: A project is due 72 hours after 9:00 AM on Monday. When is it due?
quests.hint: 72 hours is how many days?
quests.explanation: 72 hours is 3 days. Three days after Monday 9:00 AM is Thursday 9:00 AM.
quests.funFact: The word deadline once meant a line around a prison camp that prisoners were not allowed to cross.

quests.instruction: If 12 July is a Thursday, what day is 30 July?
quests.hint: Work out how many days are between the dates, then take away whole weeks.
quests.explanation: 12 July to 30 July is 18 days, which is 2 weeks and 4 days. Four days after Thursday is Monday.
quests.funFact: Stonehenge in England was probably used to follow the seasons of the year.

quests.instruction: In a leap year, how many days are there from 20 February to 10 March?
quests.hint: Count to the end of February first. Remember that it has 29 days.
quests.explanation: 20 February to 29 February is 9 days, and 29 February to 10 March is 10 more days. 9 + 10 = 19 days.
quests.funFact: Phones and computers know about leap years and add 29 February automatically.

quests.instruction: A camp starts at 9:00 AM on Wednesday and ends at 3:30 PM on Sunday. How long is the camp in days, hours and minutes?
quests.hint: Count the whole days from Wednesday 9:00 AM to Sunday 9:00 AM first.
quests.explanation: Wednesday 9:00 AM to Sunday 9:00 AM is 4 days. Then 9:00 AM to 3:30 PM is 6 hours 30 minutes. So the camp lasts 4 days 6 hours 30 minutes.
quests.funFact: Counting whole days first and then the hours is the safest way to measure a long span of time.

quests.instruction: A clock shows the short hand between 3 and 4 and the long hand on 8. A lesson started 50 minutes ago. When did it start?
quests.hint: Read the clock first, then count back 50 minutes.
quests.explanation: The long hand on 8 means 40 minutes, so the time is 3:40. 50 minutes before 3:40 is 2:50.
quests.funFact: The round face of a clock, with its numbers, is also called the dial.

quests.instruction: A digital clock shows 7:25 PM. A train left 1 hour 50 minutes ago. When did it leave?
quests.hint: Go back 1 hour first, then go back 50 more minutes.
quests.explanation: 1 hour before 7:25 PM is 6:25 PM. Going back 50 more minutes gives 5:35 PM.
quests.funFact: Sports races are often timed with electronic gates that record the exact moment a runner crosses the line.

quests.instruction: The short hand is just before the 6 and the long hand is on 11. A film lasting 1 hour 45 minutes starts at that time. When does it end?
quests.hint: Read the clock carefully: has the short hand reached the 6?
quests.explanation: The long hand on 11 means 55 minutes, and the short hand has not reached 6, so the time is 5:55. 1 hour 45 minutes later is 7:40.
quests.funFact: A lighthouse flashes its light in a pattern of seconds, so sailors can tell which lighthouse it is.

quests.instruction: A student starts a 30-minute walk at 8:55 AM and writes that it ends at 9:25 PM. What is wrong?
quests.hint: Check whether the answer still belongs to the morning.
quests.explanation: 8:55 AM plus 30 minutes is 9:25 AM. The walk starts in the morning, so it must end in the morning as well.
quests.funFact: Checking that an answer is sensible is called a reasonableness check, and scientists and engineers do it all the time.

quests.instruction: Which is the most reasonable time for baking a loaf of bread in the oven?
quests.hint: Think about whether bread bakes in a moment, in a short while, or for most of an afternoon.
quests.explanation: A loaf of bread usually bakes for about half an hour. Three minutes is far too short and three hours would burn it.
quests.funFact: Engineers often make a rough estimate first, and only then work out the exact answer.

quests.instruction: A 20-minute video starts at 3:45 PM. A pupil says it ends at 4:25 PM. What is the correct end time?
quests.hint: Count forward to 4:00 first, then add the rest.
quests.explanation: 3:45 to 4:00 is 15 minutes, and 5 more minutes makes 4:05 PM. The time 4:25 PM would be 40 minutes after the start.
quests.funFact: A calculator cannot tell you whether your question makes sense. Only you can check that.

quests.instruction: Mia starts at 4:40 PM and must finish by 6:00 PM. Plan A: homework 40 minutes, chores 25 minutes, reading 20 minutes. Plan B: homework 40 minutes, chores 20 minutes, reading 15 minutes. Which plan fits?
quests.hint: Add up each plan and count forward from 4:40.
quests.explanation: Plan A takes 85 minutes and ends at 6:05 PM, which is too late. Plan B takes 75 minutes and ends at 5:55 PM.
quests.funFact: Project managers use charts called Gantt charts to show every task on a timeline.

quests.instruction: A train leaves at 7:15 PM. It takes 18 minutes to walk to the station and 7 minutes to buy a ticket. What is the latest time to leave home?
quests.hint: Add the walk and the ticket time, then count back from 7:15.
quests.explanation: 18 + 7 = 25 minutes. 25 minutes before 7:15 PM is 6:50 PM.
quests.funFact: In many cities, the busiest travel times are around 8 in the morning and 5 in the evening.

quests.instruction: An operating room is used for two operations. Plan 1: 3:00–3:45 and 3:45–4:30. Plan 2: 3:00–3:45 and 3:40–4:30. Plan 3: 3:00–3:45 and 3:50–4:30. Which plan has a clash?
quests.hint: A clash happens when the second event starts before the first one has ended.
quests.explanation: In Plan 2 the second operation starts at 3:40, before the first ends at 3:45. In Plan 1 they meet exactly, and in Plan 3 there is a gap.
quests.funFact: Hospitals use careful schedules so that two operations are never planned for the same room at the same time.

quests.instruction: A film starts at 7:20 PM and lasts 1 hour 55 minutes. The friends must catch a bus at 9:10 PM from outside the cinema. What happens?
options: They catch it exactly on time
They catch it with 5 minutes to spare
quests.hint: Find when the film ends and compare it with 9:10.
quests.explanation: 7:20 PM plus 1 hour 55 minutes is 9:15 PM. The bus leaves at 9:10 PM, which is 5 minutes before the film ends.
quests.funFact: Cinemas leave a gap between showings so the room can be cleaned and the next audience can come in.

quests.instruction: Class A finishes at 10:45 AM. Class B starts 15 minutes later and lasts 1 hour 5 minutes. When does Class B finish?
quests.hint: Find when Class B starts first.
quests.explanation: Class B starts at 11:00 AM. 1 hour 5 minutes later is 12:05 PM.
quests.funFact: Lectures at universities often last about 50 minutes.

quests.instruction: A sign says: Open from quarter past nine in the morning to twenty to six in the evening. How long is the shop open each day?
quests.hint: Change the times said in words into digits before you count.
quests.explanation: Quarter past nine is 9:15 AM and twenty to six is 5:40 PM. 9:15 to 5:15 is 8 hours, and 5:15 to 5:40 is 25 more minutes. So the shop is open 8 hours 25 minutes.
quests.funFact: People often say times in words, such as twenty to six, even when they read them on a digital clock.

quests.instruction: A train leaves on Friday at 9:50 PM and the journey takes 7 hours 25 minutes. When does it arrive?
quests.hint: Count to midnight first. It is 2 hours 10 minutes away.
quests.explanation: 9:50 PM to midnight is 2 hours 10 minutes. The remaining 5 hours 15 minutes after midnight reach 5:15 AM, which is on Saturday.
quests.funFact: Some trains in India take more than a day and a half to travel between Kerala and the cities of the north.

quests.instruction: Option X uses three tasks of 1 hour 10 minutes, 35 minutes and 50 minutes. Option Y uses one task of 2 hours 20 minutes. Which option takes less time, and by how much?
quests.hint: Add up Option X in minutes, and then compare.
quests.explanation: Option X takes 70 + 35 + 50 = 155 minutes. Option Y takes 140 minutes. So Option Y is 15 minutes shorter.
quests.funFact: Many time-management experts suggest doing the hardest task first, when you have the most energy.

quests.instruction: A school day runs from 8:50 AM to 3:25 PM. It includes a 55-minute lunch and two 15-minute breaks. How much time is spent in lessons?
quests.hint: Find the whole school day first, then take away the lunch and both breaks.
quests.explanation: 8:50 AM to 3:25 PM is 6 hours 35 minutes, or 395 minutes. Lunch and the breaks take 55 + 15 + 15 = 85 minutes. 395 − 85 = 310 minutes, which is 5 hours 10 minutes.
quests.funFact: School days in many parts of the world last between 6 and 7 hours.
